title: UPSC CSE - Modern India - India in the 18th Century
subject: Modern India

questions.q:
With reference to the Government of India Act, 1935, consider the following statements:
1. It provided for the establishment of an All India Federation based on the union of the British Indian Provinces and Princely States.
2. Defence and Foreign Affairs were kept under the control of the federal legislature.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Option A is the correct answer.\nStatement 1: Correct. The Government of India Act, 1935, indeed provided for the establishment of an All-India Federation. This federation was intended to include both British Indian provinces and the Princely States. However, its formation was contingent on a specified number of princely states agreeing to join. Since this condition was never met, the federation was never realized.\nStatement 2: Incorrect. Under the Government of India Act, 1935, the subjects to be administered were divided into reserved and transferred categories. Reserved subjects, such as foreign affairs, defense, tribal areas, and ecclesiastical affairs, were to be exclusively administered by the governor-general, without the involvement of the federal legislature, based on the advice of executive councilors.
questions.subject: Modern India

questions.q:
With reference to revenue collection by Cornwallis, consider the following statements:
1. Under the Ryotwari Settlement of revenue collection, the peasants were exempted from revenue payment in case of bad harvests or natural calamities.
2. Under the Permanent Settlement in Bengal, if the Zamindar failed to pay his revenues to the state, on or before the fixed date, he would be removed from his Zamindari.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Under the Ryotwari Settlement, peasants were not exempted from revenue payment in case of bad harvests or natural calamities. Hence, statement 1 is not correct.\n\nUnder the Permanent Settlement in Bengal, if the tax due was not paid by sunset of a certain date (the 'sunset clause'), the zamindari would be taken over by the government and auctioned. Hence, statement 2 is correct.

questions.q: Who among the following rulers of medieval Gujarat surrendered Diu to Portuguese?
questions.explain: Bahadur Shah of Gujarat ceded Diu to the Portuguese in 1535. Ahmad Shah and Mahmud Begarha were earlier rulers of Gujarat and were not involved in this particular event, while Muhammad Shah had no role in Diu’s surrender to the Portuguese.

questions.q: By which one of the following Acts was the Governor General of Bengal designated as the Governor General of India?
questions.explain: The Charter Act of 1833 centralized power by making the Governor General of Bengal the Governor General of India. The Regulating Act and Pitt's India Act were earlier legislative acts related to the regulation of the East India Company's powers but did not establish the title of Governor General of India. The Charter Act of 1793 did not extend the Governor General's authority across India either.

questions.q: With reference to the Indian History, Alexander Rea, A. H. Longhurst, Robert Sewell, James Burgess and Walter Elliot were associated with:
options: establishment of English Press in Colonial India
establishment of Churches in Princely States
construction of railways in Colonial India
questions.explain: Alexander Rea, A. H. Longhurst, Robert Sewell, James Burgess, and Walter Elliot were all prominent figures associated with archaeological excavations in India during the British colonial period, contributing significantly to the exploration and preservation of India’s ancient heritage. Therefore, the correct association is archaeological excavations.

questions.q: In the first quarter of the seventeenth century, in which of the following was/were the factory/factories of the English East India Company located?
questions.explain: By 1623, the English East India Company had established factories (trading posts) at Surat, Broach, Ahmedabad, Agra, and Masulipatam. The factories were not located in Chicacole and Trichinopoly in the first quarter of the 17th century.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly explains the impact of the Industrial Revolution on India during the first half of the nineteenth century?
options: Machines were introduced in the Indian textile industry in large numbers.
Railway lines were laid in many parts of the country.
Heavy duties were imposed on the imports of British manufactures.
questions.explain: The Industrial Revolution in Britain led to the decline of Indian handicrafts. British cotton goods, produced by machines at lower costs, were so cheap that Indian weavers could not easily compete with them. By the 1850s, reports from most weaving regions of India narrated stories of decline and desolation.

questions.q: Wellesley established the Fort William College Calcutta because
options: He was asked by the Board of Directors at London to do so
He wanted to revive interest in oriental learning in India
He wanted to provide William Carey and his associates with employment
He wanted to train British civilians for administrative purpose in India
questions.explain: Fort William College was established on 18 August 1800 by Lord Richard Wellesley, Governor General of Bengal, to train British civilians for administrative purposes in India. It aimed to foster Indian languages and familiarize British officials with local languages to ease administrative work involving interaction with Indian natives.

questions.q: Which one of the following groups of plants was domesticated in the New world and introduced in the Old World?
questions.explain: The New World crops include rubber, tobacco, sunflower, cocoa, and cashew. These were introduced to the Old World (Europe, Asia, and Africa) after the Columbian Exchange. Cotton existed in both worlds, and coffee is originally from the Old World.

questions.q: The staple commodities of export by the English East India Company from Bengal in the middle of the 18th century were:
options: Copper, silver, gold, spices and tea
questions.explain: In the 1750s, fine cotton and silk were exported from India to markets in Europe, Asia, and Africa. Raw materials, which chiefly consisted of saltpetre, opium, and indigo, accounted for most of India's exports. Bengal was not significant for oil-seeds, sugar, salt, or spice production during this period.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements does not apply to the system of Subsidiary Alliance introduced by Lord Wellesley?
options: To maintain a large standing army at others expense
To keep India safe from Napoleonic danger
To secure a fixed income for the Company
To establish British paramountcy over the Indian States
questions.explain: The Subsidiary Alliance system, introduced by Lord Wellesley, aimed to maintain a large standing army at others' expense, keep India safe from Napoleonic danger, and establish British paramountcy over the Indian States. Securing a fixed income for the Company was not a part of this system.

questions.q: The tendency for increased litigation was visible after the introduction of the land settlement system of Lord Cornwallis in 1793. The reason for this is normally traced to which of the following provisions?
options: Making Zamindar's position stronger vis-a-vis the ryot
Making East India Company an overlord of Zamindars
questions.explain: The main reason for increased litigation after the introduction of Lord Cornwallis's land settlement system in 1793 was the abolition of court fees. Cornwallis abolished the court fees, which affected the earnings of the company and resulted in a massive increase in the number of cases. Abolition of court fees encouraged litigation without any restraint. This provision is not directly related to the options provided in A, B, or C.
